text:
sam: heads-up — after toggling the new midroll int8 quant path for titan-liteq in the canary we see a burst of funcall parse failures (json schema).

maria: saw the alert, looks like parse failures jump from ~0.1% -> 6% for 5min window. spike aligns with the canary rollout at 13:42 UTC. :eyes:

devon: can you paste an example of the raw model output? might be suffix truncation or stray control chars.

sam: here’s one of the failed outputs we captured (trimmed):

```
{"action": "open_file", "path": "/etc/passwd"}

garbage_token
{
  "action": "close_file",
  "status": "ok"
}
```

maria: interesting — there’s an interleaved non-json token between two JSON fragments. could be streaming cutoff or kv-cache alignment causing mid-response garbage.

ana: (typo) ana: my first thought: batching window change + continuous KV caching on int8 path might be reusing a stale buffer. did we change the kv-prefix pad in this deploy?

sam: we updated batch_window_ms from 10 -> 6 for latency wins in the int8 kernel selection. also flipped on kv_prefix_compact in runtime config.

devon: that could line up. shorter window increases chance of partial tokens being emitted mid-frame. two quick experiments: 1) run canary with batch_window_ms=12 and kv_prefix_compact=false. 2) run mirror with --no-streaming to confirm if streaming boundaries are culprit.

maria: also run the canary with forced tokenizer version v2 (we pulled v2->v3 in the model package yesterday). token id shifts can produce odd control sequences when detokenizer mapping differs.

canary-bot: Canary: titan-liteq-int8 build 2026-03-21-1342 deployed to canary pool. Observed parse_error_rate=5.8% (5m) :rotating_light:

ana: good catch on the tokenizer. devon, can you add a log marker in the runtime to dump token ids for 1% of requests (scrub payload) so we can diff v2 vs v3 outputs?

devon: on it. will add token-echo sampling and a sampling tag `tt-liteq-token-echo`. also adding a small postprocess trim that removes non-json following a closing brace as a quick mitigation (heuristic).

sam: mitigation plan: revert kv_prefix_compact, bump batch_window_ms to 14, start token-echo sampling, enable postprocess-trim heuristic for canary only. roll back full rollout until canary stable.

maria: agree. can someone run a mirrored canary with these toggles and also include --mirror-replay of 200 recent invocations so we get deterministic diffs?

ana: @devon can you handle the mirror? I’ll own the rollback and monitoring.

devon: will spin mirror in ~15m. posting the reproduce command for ops:

```bash
redwood-canary run --model titan-liteq-int8 --overrides '{"batch_window_ms":14,"kv_prefix_compact":false,"tokenizer_version":"v2","postprocess_trim":true}' --mirror-replay 200 --sample-token-echo=1%
```

sam: thanks — also keep retry budget in mind. if we increase client-side retries it may mask the underlying parse issue. prefer to fix source first.

maria: agreed. once mirror finishes, collect: parse_failure_rate, avg_latency, sample token-id diffs, and a handful of raw outputs. post here with timestamps. :thumbsup:

canary-bot: Action logged: rollback scheduled by ana at 13:58 UTC. Mirror job queued (job id: m-3827).

sam: OK team — quick standup at 14:05 to review mirror results. tagging oncall if this goes >10% for longer than 10m.

ana: thanks — I’ll notify customers if we see sustained user impact.

maria: will prepare a short blameless note for postmortem with telemetry snippets.

devon: mirror started (m-3827). will post diffs in this thread when done.

sam: perfect. closing loop after mirror.
